note: autoban_ban is a glue submodule of autoban: one tagged service autoban_ban.ban_provider (Drupal\autoban_ban\BanProvider) implementing AutobanProviderInterface, exposing ban-provider id 'ban' ('Core Ban', single-IP), which wraps core Ban's BanIpManager. It has no config/settings/permissions/Drush of its own. Its observable state on a live site is: the 'ban' provider appears in \Drupal::service('autoban')->getBanProvidersList(), and Autoban rules can set provider='ban'. Medium introspects a rule's provider resolved to its human name via the live provider registry; hard builds a rule wired to the core Ban provider, verified against the live config entity. Tiers: 3 easy + 2 medium + 2 hard (all three tiers present and smoke-tested). The second medium/hard pair grounds in a core-Ban rule scanning the 'access denied' log type.

evals.prompt: In the Autoban ecosystem, what does the autoban_ban submodule add, and what ban-provider id and name does it expose? What kind of ban is it (single IP or ranges)?
evals.expected_output: autoban_ban integrates Drupal core's Ban module as an Autoban ban provider with id 'ban' and name 'Core Ban'. Its ban type is 'single' (one IP at a time, no CIDR ranges); it wraps core Ban's BanIpManager.

evals.prompt: How is the core Ban provider registered so Autoban can discover it, and which class/interface implements it?
evals.expected_output: It is the service autoban_ban.ban_provider = Drupal\autoban_ban\BanProvider, tagged { name: ban_providers } and implementing Drupal\autoban\AutobanProviderInterface. Autoban's getBanProvidersList() discovers services whose id ends in '.ban_provider'. getBanIpManager() returns a core \Drupal\ban\BanIpManager.

evals.prompt: I want an Autoban rule to ban offending IPs using Drupal core's Ban module. What do I set as the rule's provider, what module must be enabled, and where do the banned IPs end up?
evals.expected_output: Set the rule's `provider` field to 'ban', with the autoban_ban submodule (and core `ban`) enabled. When the rule fires (cron / drush autoban:ban / UI), matched IPs are added to core Ban's blocked-IP list, manageable at /admin/config/people/ban.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has an Autoban rule `ab_test_banname`. Using the ban providers available on the running site, determine the human-readable NAME of the ban provider that rule uses.
evals.expected_output: Rule ab_test_banname has provider id 'ban'; resolved via \Drupal::service('autoban')->getBanProvidersList() (or the provider select), id 'ban' maps to the name 'Core Ban'.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, create an Autoban rule with machine id `autoban_test_bansub` that scans the `page not found` log type and bans offending IPs through Drupal core's Ban module after a threshold of 5. Apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: An autoban rule autoban_test_bansub exists with provider='ban' (core Ban), type='page not found', threshold=5. Because provider is the core Ban integration, matched IPs go to core Ban's list.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has an Autoban rule `ab_test_ban2` that uses Drupal core's Ban module. Inspect the live configuration and report which log type it scans and the threshold number of log entries before it bans an IP.
evals.expected_output: Rule ab_test_ban2 (provider 'ban', core Ban) scans the 'access denied' log type with threshold 15. Read it with `drush cget autoban.autoban.ab_test_ban2` (the `type` and `threshold` keys).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, create an Autoban rule with machine id `autoban_test_ban2` that scans the `access denied` log type and bans offending IPs through Drupal core's Ban module after a threshold of 9. Apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: An autoban rule autoban_test_ban2 exists with provider='ban' (core Ban), type='access denied', threshold=9. Matched IPs go to core Ban's blocked-IP list.
